case_prompt:
A 23-year-old married female, resident of Uttar Pradesh, India, was brought to the emergency department presenting with acute manic symptoms including incessant talking, elated and inappropriate affect, grandiose delusions that she was a goddess, persecutory ideas regarding family members, decreased need for sleep, marked psychomotor agitation, and muttering to herself. This behavior was followed by two generalized tonic-clonic seizures. Her past medical history was notable for first-onset seizures at age 13, for which she had received antiepileptic therapy until age 20. In addition, during the eighth month of pregnancy 7 months prior, she had experienced a depressive episode with hopelessness and crying spells that resolved following treatment with an antidepressant. There was no family history of psychiatric illness.

On physical examination, vital signs were normal. General and systemic physical examinations were unremarkable. Neurological examination showed intact cranial nerves and normal motor and sensory function. Fundoscopic examination revealed sharp disc margins without papilledema or intraocular deposits. Mental status examination revealed intense psychomotor hyperactivity, inappropriate elated affect, press of speech, decreased reaction time, elementary auditory hallucinations, grandiose delusions of divinity, and marked impairments in attention, concentration, immediate memory, recent memory, judgment, and insight, with intact abstraction. Psychological evaluation with Rorschach and Bender-Gestalt testing demonstrated findings indicative of an underlying organic etiology.

Triage laboratory testing revealed a white blood cell count of 13.1 x 10^9/L. Red blood cell count, packed cell volume, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, blood urea, serum glucose, liver function tests, and thyroid profile were all within normal limits. Baseline 12-lead electrocardiography, electroencephalography, and nerve conduction studies were normal. Plain radiographs of the skull, cervical spine, chest, forearm, and upper arm showed no abnormal calcifications.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Primary Psychiatric Disorder (Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered given the alternating polarity of a prior perinatal depressive episode followed by florid mania (grandiosity, pressured speech, insomnia), but excluded by new-onset seizures, leukocytosis, and objective psychological testing indicating an organic brain etiology.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Psychological testing, that is, Rorschach testing and Bender Gestalt revealed evidence of organic aetiology.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered as a classic infectious mimic causing mania, psychotic symptoms, cognitive deficits, and seizures, but ruled out by non-reactive serology.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Serum Venereal Disease Research Laboratory test and stool examination were negative for T. solium... Hence, the possibilities of tuberculoma, neurosyphilis and space-occupying lesion in the brain were excluded by imaging and blood tests.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered given high endemicity in India, recurrent seizures, and systemic leukocytosis, but ruled out by brain MRI demonstrating cystic lesions with eccentric scolex in the colloidal vesicular and calcified stages rather than thick-walled nodular tuberculomas or neoplasia.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The MRI showed multiple T2 hyperintense round-to-oval-shaped lesions with surrounding hyperintense signals on fluid-attenuated inversion recovery images in the bilateral cerebral hemisphere and cerebellar hemisphere as depicted in figure 1. Some of the lesions were showing eccentric nodules. No post-contrast enhancement was seen suggestive of the colloidal vesicular stage of neurocysticercosis... Hence, the possibilities of tuberculoma, neurosyphilis and space-occupying lesion in the brain were excluded by imaging and blood tests.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Confirmed by brain MRI displaying multiple bi-hemispheric cerebral and cerebellar cystic lesions with surrounding FLAIR edema, eccentric nodules (scolex) in the colloidal vesicular stage, and subsequent CT showing scattered calcified lesions in the calcified nodular stage, with symptom resolution following anticonvulsants, antipsychotics, steroids, and albendazole.
